_doc: Claude adjudication of the round-5 hunt labels, written BEFORE any case is run through any checker. Two blind sonnet judges per case (a LITERAL copy-editor lens and an ORDINARY-reader lens) labelled every case U/F/B from an anonymised, shuffled, label-free copy (workflow wf_77bf2d6f-b74). 106 of 164 were unanimous with the skeptic. The rule, fixed before any run and applied mechanically: a U case becomes B if the skeptic flagged it arguable, or EITHER judge read it as supported (F), or BOTH judges read it as either-way (B); an F case becomes B if either judge read it as unsupported or both read it as either-way; every other case keeps the skeptic's label (so a U case with one judge U and one judge B stays U). B is counted in the strict reading only, as in rounds 3 and 4. The judge prompt is round 4's, with glosses added for the five relations round 5 uses that round 4 did not (subclass_of, member_of, participant_of, located_in_time_zone, the 40-character administrative-territory property) and one sentence saying a slug drops signs and punctuation, with an example that is not in the cases.
